title: Historical telemetry curator with graceful merge and progress visibility
creator: Anita Desai
description: Build a 'telemetry curator' service that performs safe, resumable, and observable application of historical telemetry corrections to downstream analytics tables. Instead of a blind backfill, the curator will: operate on bounded time windows, produce deterministic merge artifacts, attach provenance metadata, and expose progress and dry-run views in the Console. Goals: (1) guarantee idempotent application with no double-counting across retries; (2) provide per-tenant progress and estimated cost/time; (3) allow operators to preview diffs and approve; (4) support throttling and tenant quotas to avoid production impact. Constraints: must interoperate with existing event archive (S3-raw), topic-based ingress (kafka-telemetry), and current OLAP warehouse (clickhouse-prod). We cannot change upstream event schemas. The curator produces incremental delta files and commit records; a small coordinator will atomically mark windows as committed so downstream consumers can reconcile state. Key heuristics: deterministic fingerprinting of events for de-dup, window-idempotent merge protocol, and safety watermarks to prevent overlaps.
acceptance_criteria: Can process a 7-day tenant dataset (10M events) and produce idempotent deltas that apply without changing other windows
Progress status visible in Console with start/complete/ETA and sample diff link
Dry-run mode shows summary counts and top-10 changed metrics without committing
Resumption after failure picks up from last commit token and does not double-apply
Operator approval flow (preview -> approve -> commit) implemented and tested
End-to-end test comparing reconstituted analytics against golden snapshot within 0.2% tolerance for key metrics
updates: 2025-02-10: Ticket created. Initial design with windowed processing and deterministic hashing. Assigned to Liam.

2025-02-18: Spike completed — validated deterministic fingerprint approach using SHA256 over normalized event payload. Observed 1.8x CPU cost relative to current ingest but within budget for curator batch windows.

2025-02-24: Decision: use S3 for intermediate delta shards and a small Kafka topic (telemetry-curation-ledger) for commit records to preserve provenance and enable fast lookup. Rationale: S3 gives cheaper storage for large windows and ledger enables atomic visibility to Console.
2025-02-27: Design review feedback from PM/Observability: add tenant-level throttles and a safety circuit breaker when ClickHouse latency > 200ms. Added to implementation notes.
2025-03-03: Implemented dry-run summary generator and basic Console endpoint. Open PR for curator worker scaffolding: GH#https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-curator/pull/72

2025-03-04: Early integration test revealed an edge case where late-arriving events with identical fingerprints from overlapping windows caused duplicate correction attempts. Plan: embed window-start in fingerprint salt and add validation during commit to reject duplicates.
implementation_notes: Worker model: coordinator (assign windows) + worker (produce deltas) + applier (safe-apply path)
Delta format: newline-delimited JSON with fingerprint, original_event_id, tenant_id, event_ts, corrected_fields, source_window_id
Commit ledger: kafka topic with message {window_id, delta_s3_path, fingerprint_set_path, commit_ts, operator_id}
Idempotency: apply operation will check commit ledger and fingerprint set before mutating warehouse; fingerprint set persisted as bloom filter + small manifest for verification
Visibility: Console shows sample diffs stored in S3 (signed URLs), and a progress object pulled from ledger with counts and ETA
Safety: stop applying if ClickHouse write latency spikes or error rate exceeds 2% for 5 minutes; require manual restart after safety event
Cost estimation: worker emits estimated token/row count and projected ClickHouse write cost; Console surfaces estimate before operator approval
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: double-counting due to overlapping windows — Mitigation: include window salt in fingerprint and strong commit-time validation
Risk: large tenant jobs impacting warehouse performance — Mitigation: tenant-scoped quotas and traffic shaping with graceful backoff
Risk: schema drift in historical events — Mitigation: normalize at fingerprinting stage and abort window with drift report for manual triage
Risk: operator confusion — Mitigation: add clear UX states (dry-run, pending-approval, applying, committed) and provide sample diffs + metric deltas
qa_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint determinism and window-salt behavior
Integration test that runs curator against synthetic archive and compares metrics before/after with golden snapshot
Chaos test: kill worker mid-window and assert resumption correctness and no double-apply
Performance test: run on 10M-event tenant and measure CPU, S3 usage, ClickHouse writes, and end-to-end time
